findings.evidence: tests/test_platform_module_identity.py: test_identity_holds_in_forward_and_reverse_import_order (subprocess.run ... timeout=600 per order); direct_registrations only matches ast.Assign/AugAssign/AnnAssign subscripts and the update/setdefault/__setitem__ calls; test_platform_module_identity is listed in [test_groups.fast-c] in dev-platform/checks.toml.
findings.summary: The forward/reverse import guard imports every test module twice in fresh subprocesses with a 600s timeout, and it runs inside the parallel fast-c group. It adds wall-clock to the critical path and depends on all test modules being import-safe. The static scanner also only flags `sys.modules[...] =` and update/setdefault/__setitem__; `sys.modules.pop`, `del` and `setattr` bypass it.

findings.evidence: template/scripts/affected_test_groups.py _string_references: `if IDENTIFIER.fullmatch(node.value): names.add(node.value)`; affected_groups: `not direct_test and stem in references[module]` selects all importers of a changed helper.
findings.summary: The affected map treats any string constant that is a bare identifier as a module reference, and a changed tests/ helper (for example tests/_platform_modules.py) selects every importing test module. Over-selection is harmless to correctness. Under-selection is possible for modules referenced only through dynamic names or transitive imports, which the design accepts. The precheck is feedback only and the full set always runs, so this is not blocking.
